title: The gradient for B, checked by a nudge
starter:
%a  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=0
%b  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=1
%o  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=2
%va = load %a
%vb = load %b
%A  = reshape %va [2 2]
%B  = reshape %vb [2 2]
%gf = reshape %B [4]
%st = store %o %gf
%o1 = after %o %st
hints: Build the loss first, the same three lines as the exercise before this one: `matmul`, a `reshape` to `[4]`, then `reduce` with `op=add`.
Ask for `gradient %L %B`. It has B's shape, 2x2, so reshape it to `[4]` before the store.
`%C = matmul %A %B`, `%f = reshape %C [4]`, `%L = reduce %f op=add`, `%g = gradient %L %B`, then change the last reshape to `%gf = reshape %g [4]`.
explain: Nudge `B[0][0]` by 1. It is multiplied by `A[0][0]` in `C[0][0]` and by `A[1][0]` in `C[1][0]`, so L moves by `A[0][0] + A[1][0]`, the sum of column 0 of A. The same holds for `B[0][1]`. Row 1 of B gets the sum of column 1 of A. For A = `[[1 2] [3 4]]` that is `[4 4 6 6]`. You wrote no rule for matmul. The backward walk went through its reduce, mul, expand and reshape, one partner at a time.
